rules.name: Overview
rules.desc: Students must complete introductory courses in communication theory and research, research methods, and pedagogy. These core courses are grounded in social science literature and emphasize how people respond to media and how media institutions function. In addition, PhD students must complete three substantive COMM courses designed for PhD students and another three graduate level COMM courses taught by PhD program faculty.

children.name: Advanced Methods Coursework
children.desc: Two advanced research methods courses approved by the academic advisor and the DGS. The following courses are preapproved: course and course.
children.notes: Courses cannot be double counted as both a substantive and a research methods course. Courses must be completed by the end of Spring quarter of year 2 with grades of ‘B’ or above.

children.name: Substantive Coursework
children.desc: Three substantive COMM courses designed for PhD students (e.g., 300-level seminars) from three different Communication PhD faculty and another three different graduate level COMM courses from COMM PhD faculty by the end of Spring quarter of year.

children.name: Area Exam
children.desc: The Area Exam is an opportunity to demonstrate proficiency in tools required in the student’s area of research specialization by passing a one-week take-home area exam followed by a one-hour oral exam by the end of spring quarter of year 4. The area exam is a critical assessment of the student’s knowledge in their research area and their ability to produce a dissertation. Identified with the advice of the faculty, the content of the area exam may include detailed theoretical knowledge, advanced statistical methods, ethnographic or archival skills, a foreign language, computer programming, or other technical skills. Because the multifaceted nature of the department makes it possible for the PhD student to specialize in areas that draw on different related disciplines, the Area Exam is individualized and developed between the faculty advisor and the student.
children.notes: More detail about the Area Examination can be found in the Department of Communication’s Degree Requirements & Department Procedures for Ph.D. Students and Ph.D. Advisors.

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc: Teaching is core to the academic and professional training of PhD students in our program. As such, all students must complete three quarters of teaching experience in courses offered by the Department of Communication to fulfill degree requirements regardless of financial support. Many communication students complete more than the required number of teaching experience quarters as part of their financial support and professional training.

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc:
Research is core to the academic and professional training of PhD students in our program. Complete at least two pre-dissertation research projects. The Major Project and the Minor Project are research papers, primarily authored by the student, that are considered to be of sufficient quality to be publishable in a respected journal. The projects do not have to be completed in any specific order.
The Major Project must meet the APA guideline for first authorship, providing an opportunity for the student to demonstrate that they are able to successfully and independently perform all relevant aspects of a research project by developing the research questions, conducting the research, and writing the paper.
The Minor Project must meet the APA guidelines for authorship, providing an opportunity for the student to demonstrate that they have gained significant experience in all relevant aspects of a research project in collaboration with a faculty advisor by playing a major role developing the research questions, conducting the research, and writing the paper.
Students are required to complete their first project by the end of winter quarter of year 3, and their second by the end of winter quarter of year 4.
The Project Readers (the Project Advisor and another Academic Council member) are selected by the student and approved by the student’s advisor. The Project Readers will determine if the student has passed the project. A student failing to complete either the Major or Minor Project requirement may be dismissed from the program.
See the Department of Communication’s Degree Requirements & Department Procedures for Ph.D. Students and Ph.D. Advisors for detailed information.

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc:
Advancement to candidacy is a prospective judgement by the faculty in the degree program of the student’s potential to successfully complete the requirements of the degree program.
Students are required to apply for candidacy by the end of the first week of Spring quarter of the student’s second year. The evaluation for candidacy is based on the performance in the development of the Major and/or Minor Project and in the required courses as well as the quality of final papers for the core seminars, COMM 302A, B, C. The student’s application to candidacy will be reviewed by the PhD faculty as a whole by the end of the Spring quarter of the second year. PhD candidacy is valid for five years.
See the Department of Communication’s Degree Requirements & Department Procedures for Ph.D. Students and Ph.D. Advisors for detailed information.

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc: In the Department of Communication, the Oral Exam is a defense of the dissertation presented upon the completion of a substantial portion of the dissertation or upon completion of the pre-final draft. Students consult with their dissertation advisor and reading committee members on the timing of the defense.

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc:
Students complete a dissertation proposal document describing the research plan for the dissertation thereby clearly specifying the concepts and theories, literature(s), method(s) and data sources, and analysis strategy. All members of the student’s Dissertation Reading Committee attend the proposal meeting to assess and approve the proposal.
The proposal meeting, attended by all members of the student’s Dissertation Reading Committee, is based on a dissertation proposal document describing the research plan for the dissertation, clearly specifying the concepts and theories, literature(s), method(s) and data sources, and analysis strategy. Subsequent to the proposal meeting, the student is responsible for revising the proposal document and receiving approval from the reading committee.
Students complete a dissertation satisfactory to a reading committee composed of three or more faculty members in the Department of Communication and one outside the Department of Communication.
